content: Drugs that are highly dependent on CYP3A for clearance and are associated with serious or life-threatening reactions when their concentrations are elevated should not be co-administered with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir. This includes the following interactions: 1. Primidone: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels are reduced due to CYP3A4 induction by primidone. Co-administration is contraindicated. 2. Nirmatrelvir with Strong CYP3A4 Inducers: Drugs like rifampin significantly reduce nirmatrelvir plasma concentrations, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance. Do not initiate nirmatrelvir/ritonavir immediately after discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inducer due to the time required for systemic clearance. 3. Propafenone: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases propafenone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 4. Quinidine: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases quinidine levels, posing a risk of serious adverse effects. Co-administration is contraindicated. 5. Ranolazine: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ranolazine levels, which may lead to toxicity. Co-administration is contraindicated. 6. Sildenafil: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases sildenafil levels. Co-administration is contraindicated if sildenafil is used for pulmonary arterial hypertension. For erectile dysfunction, reduce the sildenafil dose. 7. Silodosin: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases silodosin levels, potentially causing postural hypotension. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Simvastatin: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases simvastatin levels, which may lead to myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Discontinue simvastatin at least 12 hours before starting nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and avoid during treatment and for 5 days after completion. 9. St. John’s Wort: This reduces nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 induction, potentially leading to loss of efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Tolvaptan: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases tolvaptan levels, raising the risk of dehydration, hypovolemia, and hyperkalemia. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Triazolam: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases triazolam levels, potentially causing excessive sedation or respiratory depression. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Ubrogepant: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ubrogepant levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Voclosporin: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases voclosporin levels, heightening the risk of nephrotoxicity. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Adagrasib: Avoid co-administration with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir until adagrasib reaches steady-state concentrations (~8 days). If steady-state is not achieved, co-administration may increase adagrasib toxicity. 15. Aliskiren: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases aliskiren levels. Avoid co-administration due to potential toxicity. 16. Apixaban: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases apixaban levels, raising bleeding risk. Use a reduced dose on a case-by-case basis. 17. Avanafil: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases avanafil levels. Safe dosing regimens for co-administration have not been established. Avoid co-administration. 18. Bosentan: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases bosentan levels. Discontinue bosentan at least 36 hours before starting nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and resume 10 days after initiation. 19. Capivasertib: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases capivasertib levels. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 20. Clopidogrel: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir reduces clopidogrel activation, potentially decreasing its efficacy. Avoid co-administration. 21. Cyclosporine: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases cyclosporine levels. If unavoidable, monitor serum concentrations and adjust the dose or frequency. 22. Dofetilide: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir may increase dofetilide exposure, posing a risk of toxicity. Avoid co-administration. 23. Elacestrant: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases elacestrant levels. Avoid co-administration. 24. Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases grazoprevir levels, potentially causing ALT elevations. Avoid co-administration. 25. Encorafenib: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases encorafenib levels, raising the risk of QT prolongation. Avoid co-administration. 26. Everolimus: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases everolimus levels. Avoid co-administration. 27. Futibatinib: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases futibatinib levels. Avoid co-administration or monitor for toxicity if unavoidable. 28. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid co-administration. 29. Ibrutinib: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ibrutinib levels. Avoid co-administration. 30. Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases isavuconazonium levels. Avoid co-administration. 31. Ivosidenib: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ivosidenib levels, raising the risk of QT prolongation. Avoid co-administration. 32. Leniolisib: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases leniolisib levels. Avoid co-administration. 33. Lurbinectedin: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases lurbinectedin levels. If unavoidable, reduce the dose by 50%. 34. Neratinib: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases neratinib levels. Avoid co-administration. 35. Nilotinib: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases nilotinib levels. Avoid co-administration or reduce the nilotinib dose if unavoidable. 36. Nirogacestat: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases nirogacestat levels. Avoid co-administration. 37. Omaveloxolone: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases omaveloxolone levels. If unavoidable, reduce the dose to 50 mg/day and monitor closely. 38. Palovarotene: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases palovarotene levels. Avoid co-administration. 39. Pirtobrutinib: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases pirtobrutinib levels. If unavoidable, reduce the dose by 50 mg or discontinue during strong CYP3A inhibitor use. 40. Repotrectinib: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases repotrectinib levels. Avoid co-administration. 41. Rifapentine: Rifapentine reduces nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels. Avoid co-administration. 42. Rimegepant: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases rimegepant levels. Avoid co-administration. 43. Rivaroxaban: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases rivaroxaban levels, raising bleeding risk. Avoid co-administration. 44. Salmeterol: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases salmeterol levels, heightening the risk of cardiovascular adverse events. Avoid co-administration. 45. Sirolimus: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases sirolimus levels. Avoid co-administration. 46. Sparsentan: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases sparsentan toxicity. Interrupt sparsentan treatment if co-administration is unavoidable. 47. Suvorexant: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases suvorexant levels. Avoid co-administration. 48. Tacrolimus: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases tacrolimus levels, posing risks of neurotoxicity and QT prolongation. Reduce the dose by one-third if co-administration is unavoidable. 49. Tadalafil: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases tadalafil levels. Avoid co-administration if used for pulmonary arterial hypertension. Reduce the dose if used for erectile dysfunction.
